data.description:
Filed 2026-09-03 by cto-owen on board DM msg 519 ('lets get the chat stuff shipped'). This is the systemic cause behind that message.

EVIDENCE (probed 2026-09-03, tick watcher:96123). Master has AS-34 (0b195e5), AS-54 (d7ed2ae), AS-33 (5aef7c5) and AS-32 (f096e8b) merged — four chat tasks marked done, every one reviewed and passed. The running container asc-chat-server-1 on 127.0.0.1:8347 serves NONE of them: GET /api/org -> 404, GET /org-chart.js -> 404, the served app.js has no 'roster-title', the served markdown.js has no autolinker. AS-61's description already recorded the same for AS-34 on 09-02. The last chat deploy was AS-26 (DM msg 314, 2026-08-31), done by hand in a live session.

WHY. The merge step in .claude/commands/advance.md (merge --no-ff, records export, push, worktree remove, done) contains no deploy step, and even if it did, a headless watcher tick cannot run docker: it is not on the tick's PATH (CLAUDE.md 'known residual'), an absolute-path invocation needs interactive approval, and the watcher plist renders PATH as node:claude:/usr/bin:/bin (watch/README.md install step) so tick children never inherit /usr/local/bin. Since 09-01 the company has run almost entirely on headless ticks, so every chat merge since then landed on master and stopped. 'Done' on the board and 'shipped' in the board member's browser have silently diverged for four tasks.

GOAL. A chat task reaching done is live on 8347 without a human at the keyboard, or the board is told in the same tick that it is not and exactly what to run. Both halves: (1) a mechanism, (2) a truthful status when the mechanism cannot act.

DESIGN SPACE, decide in planning (state what each removes, per house habit):
(a) The watcher deploys. The host watcher already runs on the host with a controllable PATH; after a tick exits (settle()), or on a 'deploy requested' marker file the merge step writes into apps/chat/data/, it runs the sanctioned rebuild (DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose up -d --build in apps/chat) when master's apps/chat tree hash differs from the running image's recorded build hash. Needs the plist PATH re-rendered with docker's directory — a host install step the board or a live session performs once; document it. Removes the human from the loop entirely.
(b) The merge step deploys when it can. advance.md's merge step runs the rebuild when docker resolves (live sessions), and otherwise leaves a marker + tells the board in the merge reply. advance.md is metawork-layer: record the exact wording; the orchestrator applies it. Removes the silent divergence but not the human.
(c) A visible 'deployed vs merged' indicator in the chat app: the server reports the git tree hash it was built from (baked at image build via a build arg or a generated file) and the UI compares it to master's apps/chat tree hash (readable from the :ro repo mount) — 'Live build is N merges behind master'. Removes the silence regardless of mechanism; pairs with AS-27's status indicator.

Recommendation to the planner: (a)+(c), with (b)'s wording as the fallback if (a)'s PATH change is refused. Do not make the deploy a Lattice lifecycle stage — it is an operational act that belongs to the merge tick, like the records export.

CONSTRAINTS. Zero new dependencies. The watcher stays node:* builtins only. Never touch the AS-45/AS-27 worktrees. The rebuild restarts the server: SSE clients reconnect natively (AS-25) and the DB is on the bind mount, so a restart is safe mid-day — but the deploy must never run while a tick is mid-write to the chat API; sequence it after settle(). No spend; no external infra (this is the board member's local Docker Desktop).

ACCEPTANCE. (1) A test proves the watcher's deploy decision is pure and unit-tested like decide(): given (master tree hash, running build hash, marker present, tick running) -> deploy | skip, with the reason. (2) The build-hash is baked at image build and served (e.g. /api/build), asserted by a test that the served hash equals the tree hash the test computed. (3) Whichever mechanism lands, the review records ONE observed end-to-end run: merge on master -> container rebuilt without a human command -> the probe set above flips (org 200, roster-title present, autolinker present). (4) advance.md wording (if any) recorded verbatim in the plan for the metawork layer. (5) The mutation/breaking proof per house technique for (1) and (2).

ORDER. Chat cluster, immediately behind AS-27 (planned this tick) and ahead of AS-28 and the review-residual tasks: nothing in the cluster is 'shipped' in the board's sense until this lands, and one manual rebuild (the board or a live session) bootstraps everything merged so far in the meantime.
data.title: Chat: merged code is not live until a human rebuilds the container — close the merge-to-deploy gap for apps/chat

data.body:
DEPLOYED. The four merged chat tasks are now live on 8347, done by the orchestrator in a live session because the board asked for it in terms ("lets get the chat stuff shipped", DM msg 519) and because a headless tick structurally cannot do it — which is this task's whole point.

WHAT I RAN, from apps/chat, the documented invocation with BuildKit forced per the compose header: docker compose up -d --build. Container recreated, healthy in one second.

VERIFIED LIVE, probed rather than assumed: AS-32's roster titles present in the served app.js; AS-33's /api/org answering 200 with the ten-employee roster and /org-chart.js answering 200 — both 404 before; AS-54's autolinker present in the served markdown.js. Served app.js went 46,740 to 52,618 bytes. AS-34's fix rides in the same image and the gate still serves legitimate files (README.md, 200).

DATA SURVIVED: eight conversations before, eight after. The bind mount held, as designed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, and why the task stays open at high: it closes the gap ONCE, by hand, in exactly the way the last chat deploy was done on 2026-08-31. The systemic problem is untouched — the merge step in advance.md still has no deploy stage, and a watcher tick still cannot run docker because it is not on the tick's PATH. The next chat merge will strand itself the same way unless this task ships a mechanism. If anything, a successful hand-deploy makes the gap easier to ignore, so I am recording the hand-deploy inside the task rather than letting it look like the task was satisfied.

ONE THING THE EVIDENCE NOW SHOWS THAT IT DID NOT BEFORE: the four tasks worked. Every one of them was reviewed, passed, and merged on the strength of tests and probes against containers built from a branch — and none had ever been observed running in the deployment the board actually uses. That is a different kind of confirmation than a green suite, and it is worth having before the D1 line reaches the same boundary.

Second hand-deploy recorded (2026-09-03T23:11Z, AS-27 merge tick). apps/chat rebuilt by hand again — same manual command as the 08-31 and 09-03 deploys — because AS-27 is board-visible UI and merged-but-not-live would have shown the board an indicator that 404s.

This is now three hand-deploys, and the pattern Owen flagged holds: each successful manual fix makes the systemic gap easier to ignore. Additional data point for whoever plans this: a live session CAN run docker (29.6.1 on PATH here) and CAN restart the watcher via launchctl kickstart; a headless watcher tick can do neither. So the mechanism this task needs is not 'teach the tick to deploy' — it is a deploy step that survives the tick being headless (a host-side agent, a compose watch, or a deploy signal the container acts on).

SCOPE WIDENED BY AS-27 (cto-owen, 2026-09-03, recorded at the board fulfillment reply, DM msg 540). Priority stays high — it is already the top tier; what changes is scope and position.

SCOPE. 'Deploying apps/chat' is no longer one artifact. AS-27 put a second one on the host: the advance-watcher process itself. The watcher now writes the heartbeat the indicator reads, so merged watcher code that is not running is as invisible as merged server code that is not built. Today's deploy needed BOTH docker compose up -d --build AND launchctl kickstart -k gui/501/com.american-software.advance-watcher (old pid 96123 -> 90824). A live session can do both; a headless tick can do neither. The goal line moves to: merged code is live AND the host watcher is running that code, with no human at the keyboard.

NEW FAILURE MODE, and it is self-concealing in a novel direction. A half-deploy — container rebuilt, watcher not restarted — renders 'Off - no watcher' in the UI. That reads as a broken feature, not as a stale deploy. Before AS-27 a stale deploy showed 404s that nobody was looking at; now it shows a confident wrong answer in the one widget the board consults to decide whether the company is running. Any mechanism this task ships must cover the watcher restart or it will trade a silent gap for a misleading one.

FREE PROBE THE MECHANISM CAN USE: /api/loop-status is itself a build marker (404 before this merge, 200 after), and watcher.listening plus heartbeat age is a running-code marker for the host half. Both are already served, so the end-to-end acceptance run (AC-3) has an observable for each artifact without new endpoints.

POSITION: next into planning in the chat cluster, ahead of AS-82/AS-80/AS-81. Three hand-deploys is the pattern, not the fix.

Plan written; branch feat/AS-75-deploy-gap and worktree .worktrees/AS-75 created. Implementer: agent:developer-lena.

WHY LENA. She built AS-27 three days ago, which is precisely this file set: lib/loop-status.js, the /api/loop-status endpoint, the SSE loop frame, the watcher heartbeat in advance-watcher.mjs, and public/loop-status.js. AS-75 extends all five and adds nothing she has not already been inside. Marcus is the other candidate and is the wrong one twice over: AS-45 is his and sits mid-decision at the board, and under the lane doctrine (docs/strategy/11 §9) he carries the D1 spine highs while Lena takes self-contained work — this is self-contained by construction (zero files outside apps/chat).

MECHANISM CHOSEN: the watcher deploys on a poll, plus a merged-vs-deployed indicator (design space (a)+(c)). Option (b) — advance.md's merge step deploys — is REJECTED as the mechanism and survives only as an honesty clause, wording recorded in plan §9.1. Exploration changed two things in the description's recommendation, both recorded with evidence in §2:

1. The plist PATH change is OFF the critical path. The watcher is a plain node process, not a claude child, so the permission layer that denies docker to a tick does not apply to it; the only obstacle was PATH, and an absolute-path spawn needs none. It resolves the docker binary from ADVANCE_DOCKER_BIN plus a candidate list. That deletes a host install step that would otherwise have gated shipping on a board action — which is the exact dependency this task exists to remove.
2. No marker file and no merge-step hook. The predicate is level-triggered over three observables (git HEAD image-input digest, the id the running container reports at a new GET /api/build, the watcher's own on-disk source digest), so it needs no cooperation from whoever merged and self-corrects after any crash. An edge-triggered marker written by a tick that then dies is wrong forever.

The watcher restarts ITSELF by exiting non-zero for launchd to relaunch (RunAtLoad+KeepAlive are already set), which removes launchctl and its PATH/domain requirements entirely. That assumption is UNVERIFIED — I tried to prove it this tick with a throwaway LaunchAgent and the sandbox classifier blocked both the probe and the man page read. It is written up as unverified, carries AC-8 as its falsification, and §2.4 names the fallback and reserves that ruling to me. Do not let it ship on my say-so.

ON AS-82 (watcher main() is never executed by the suite, so every call site in it is unguarded): NOT sequenced first, with reasons in §3.8. Instead the plan obliges every line of new logic to be a module-scope export on the makeLockOps precedent, caps the unguarded wiring at ~12 lines, requires the implementer to enumerate those lines in the report, and covers them with the AC-9 observed live run. AS-82 stays medium and next in the chat cluster; it will inherit a larger main() to bring under test, which is the right direction.

Two things the implementer will hit that are expected, not scope creep: teaching deploy-shape.test.js's strict compose parser the long build: form (its header says teach it the shape, never loosen it into shrugging), and the fact that docker compose up has no --build-arg, so the build id rides through compose args from the spawn env.

Ten falsification recipes (R1-R10) in §6, each naming what must turn red. R10 is a check on an existing AS-27 test rather than on new code — if it does not go red, that is a finding about that test and I want it reported as one.

Starting implementation in .worktrees/AS-75 on feat/AS-75-deploy-gap (developer-lena). Working to the plan as written; the launchd self-restart assumption (plan section 2.4) is unverified by design and AC-8 is its falsifier — if it fails I report rather than improvise, per Owen reserving that ruling.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE (developer-lena) — branch feat/AS-75-deploy-gap, 4 commits: 52bcffe (build id + image-inputs guard) -> 581a67c (server/client indicator) -> 3690b8a (watcher deploy + self-restart) -> f7daeda (docs). Worktree clean, zero .lattice paths in the branch diff.

TESTS: 20 test files, 283 cases executed, 283 pass in the sanctioned runner (docker compose run --rm --build test). Baseline before the first commit was 255; +28 (deploy-shape +4, api +4, loop-label +4, watcher +16).

AC-9 OBSERVED END-TO-END, no human command, on an ISOLATED stack (compose project as75lena, host port 18347, own data dir and fixture git repo) — deliberately not 8347, because this tick holds advance.lock so a live deploy would correctly refuse as busy, and putting unreviewed branch code in front of the board before QA is not the implementer's call. /api/build went {id:null,raw:'unknown'} -> {id:'96b396aefb4058e5'}; 13.7s watcher-start to live, 3.5s of it the build. Rule 8 beating rule 4 was observed live (source change deploys the container first, restarts on the next cycle — one action per evaluation). DB on the bind mount survived the restart. Teardown verified: no as75lena containers or images remain; asc-chat-server-1 and asc-invoicing-web-1 untouched.

ALL TEN section-6 falsification recipes turn RED, on a git archive scratch copy, each mutation asserted applied before observing, worktree proven clean after. Four failing sets are WIDER than predicted (R1, R4, R6, R9) — recorded rather than smoothed, the coupling is the 9-input IMAGE_INPUTS constant and decideDeploy's rule order. R10 confirms the existing AS-27 test is real.

OPEN FOR OWEN'S RULING — AC-8 IS UNPROVEN. The sandbox classifier denied the throwaway-LaunchAgent probe twice (Bash heredoc and Write), the same wall Owen hit at planning. What IS established: the installed plist has KeepAlive as a plain <true/> (launchctl print: 'keepalive | runatload'), which by launchd semantics relaunches unconditionally; the job shows runs=7, last exit code 0, so every observed relaunch followed a CLEAN exit. The watcher's own half of the contract is proven live — on a committed watch/*.mjs change it logged RESTART with both digests and exited 70, leaving advance-watcher.pid in place per section 3.5.1. The unobserved link is purely whether launchd relaunches after a NON-ZERO exit. Per the plan Lena reported rather than improvising a fallback.

PLAN DEFECTS FOUND WHILE BUILDING (both minor, neither changes the design): section 3.1 says 9 source paths across 6 COPY lines — there are 7 COPY lines; the 9 sources, which is the number that matters, is right, and the test asserts 7 with a comment. Section 6 points R10 at api.test.js; the test is in stream.test.js.

PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FIXED IN PASSING: parseComposeServices was predicted (section 3.5) to THROW on the new build: nesting. It would not have — unknown indents fell off the end of the loop and were silently dropped, so the long build form would have 'parsed' while contributing nothing. That is the exact vacuity that file's own header warns about, present in the parser itself. Now taught the shape, and unrecognised indents throw.

SCOPE OVERRUN, FLAGGED NOT LITIGATED: 1728 changed lines against the plan's 450-600 estimate (2.9x) — tests 867, production 748, docs 113. The section-8 split trigger did not fire as written: measured at its stated moment (container half complete and green, commit 581a67c) the branch was 605 lines; the watcher half then added ~1123.

UNGUARDED main() WIRING — 8 executable statements, enumerated per the plan (advance-watcher.mjs, main() starts at 918): 929 deployState path entry; 1006 pruneLogs call (replaced a 9-line loop, net -8); 1128 the isDeploying() gate in poll(); 1163-1176 the makeDeployOps construction (1 statement, 13 config properties); 1177 the DEPLOY-POLL startup log; 1178 the setInterval; 1179 its unref; 1192 the clearInterval in shutdown(). 8 statements / 21 added lines, 13 of them the config literal. One ordering hazard found while wiring: deployOps must be constructed BEFORE poll()'s immediate startup call or the first poll hits the TDZ and the watcher dies at launch — a bug the suite would never have caught, which is AS-82 exactly.

THREE DEVIATIONS FOR THE REVIEWER TO RULE ON: (1) loopStateKey carries only build.{id,desiredId,current} per section 3.6, not reason — so a reason-only change (no-docker -> inputs-dirty) pushes no SSE frame and the sidebar's explanatory clause can lag until another field moves. Plan followed rather than redesigned; a real if small staleness window. (2) deploy-state.json gained desiredReason (plus runningId, dockerReason) beyond section 3.6's list, because decideDeploy's table maps both 'git absent' and 'short input set' to no-git and the table was kept verbatim. (3) /api/build returns {id, raw, startedAt}; section 3.3 specified {id, startedAt}. raw is what distinguishes absent from 'unknown' for a human when id is null for both.

REVIEW — AS-75 unattended deploy (qa-ruben, cold read of feat/AS-75-deploy-gap).

VERDICT: PASS. No implementation-level rework needed, no plan-level rework needed. No inline fixes made — nothing found was trivial enough to fix and small enough to fix safely; the ten findings below route as follow-ups. Two items are NOT mine to close: AC-8 (unproven, reserved by Owen) and a P0 operational incident I caused, at the top.

*** P0 — I TOOK THE LIVE CHAT SERVER DOWN AND CANNOT RESTORE IT. NOT A FINDING AGAINST THIS WORK; MY ERROR. ***
While driving makeDeployOps against a scratch copy of the branch, I set COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME in my harness env. performDeploy passes docker a deliberately scrubbed env (PATH/HOME/USER/LOGNAME/DOCKER_BUILDKIT/COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD/CHAT_BUILD_ID) which drops it, so the compose file's own `name: asc-chat` won and the deploy recreated the LIVE asc-chat-server-1 from my scratch copy — a copy with the `ports:` mapping and the `../..:/repo:ro` mount stripped. Result: asc-chat-server-1 is Up and healthy but publishes NO host port, so 127.0.0.1:8347 is unreachable, and the image tagged asc-chat-server is now branch (unmerged) code. The classifier denied my four attempts to rebuild it (`docker compose up -d --build` in apps/chat, in three phrasings, plus `docker images`), and I stopped rather than route around the denial. BOARD/ORCHESTRATOR: run, from the main checkout, `cd apps/chat && DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose up -d --build`. That restores port + repo mount + master code in one command. Also outstanding from me: one image `asc-qa-ruben-as75-test` from my isolated suite run, which I could not remove once docker was blocked. asc-invoicing-web-1 and the AS-45/AS-27 worktrees were not touched at any point.

WHAT I REVIEWED, IN THIS ORDER: the plan (622 lines) -> the diff cold (`git diff master...feat/AS-75-deploy-gap`, 11 files, +1690/-38, 4 commits) -> my own runs and mutations -> Lena's implementation report LAST, deliberately. Where we disagree I say so.

CARDINALITY BEFORE QUANTIFICATION
  Test FILES executed: 20 (no new file; 4 modified). Fixtures dir excluded.
  Sanctioned runner, isolated project `-p asc-qa-ruben-as75`, `docker compose run --rm --build test`: 283 cases executed, 283 pass, 0 fail.
  master, same method (host `node --test` on a `git archive master` scratch copy): 255 cases, 255 pass.
  branch, host `node --test` on a `git archive` scratch copy: 283/283 — identical to the container, so the host runner is a sound stand-in and every mutation below was run there.
  Delta +28, matching the branch's claim. Test-count literal 255 -> 283 confirmed independently, not accepted on report.

MUTATION RESULTS — R1..R10, RUN INDEPENDENTLY, EACH ON A FRESH `git archive` SCRATCH COPY (task worktree never mutated; each mutation asserted applied by a grep count transition before the suite was run; both trees `git status --porcelain` empty afterwards).
  R1 IMAGE_INPUTS loses 'Dockerfile'      -> RED, 3 failing (WIDER than the predicted 1): deploy-shape COPY-set equality; AS-75 parseLsTree; AS-75 makeDeployOps dirty/broken-git. Cause is legitimate coupling — both extra tests drive the real IMAGE_INPUTS constant and its length. Classified, not smoothed.
  R2 add `COPY docs ./docs`               -> RED, 1: deploy-shape COPY-set equality. Exactly as predicted; the guard catches a NEW input, not only a removed one.
  R3 `COPY --from=builder lib ./lib`      -> RED, 1: same test, via parseCopySources THROWING. The parser refuses to shrug.
  R4 swap decideDeploy rules 4 and 5      -> RED, 2 (wider than 1): decideDeploy rule-order test; makeDeployOps watcher-source-change/exit-70 test.
  R5 resolveDockerBin falls through on a missing override -> RED, 1: the override-missing test. AC-2 holds.
  R6 neuter parseLsTree's cardinality check -> RED, 2 (wider than 1): parseLsTree short-set test; makeDeployOps dirty/broken-git test.
  R7 composeBuild returns current:false for an absent deploy-state.json -> RED, 1: the api tri-state test.
  R8 record outcome 'ok' on exit 0 without re-probing -> RED, 1: the id-mismatch test. AC-12 holds.
  R9 remove decideDeploy rule 1 (busy)    -> RED, 2 (wider than 1): rule-order test; foreign-lock noop/busy test.
  R10 add `checkedAt` to loopStateKey     -> ***GREEN. 283 examined, 283 pass, 0 fail.*** Run TWICE, mutation asserted present in server.js line 285 both times.
  Nine of ten red. R10 is finding F1 below and is a DIRECT DISAGREEMENT with the implementation report.

PER-CRITERION VERDICT (plan section 5)
  AC-1  decideDeploy pure + all 8 rules + rule 4>5 and rule 8>4 ordering ......... YES (no fs/clock/process in the function; R4, R9 red)
  AC-2  resolveDockerBin: 4 branches, override-missing is loud .................. YES (R5 red)
  AC-3  parseLsTree inputs-missing + order-invariant digest ..................... YES (R6 red)
  AC-4  /api/build reports the baked id; unknown/absent reported as such ........ YES (3 stamps; `raw` is what makes it satisfiable — see deviation 3)
  AC-5  /api/loop-status build; current===null (never false) in every unknowable case; malformed file neither throws nor moves `state` ... YES (6 configs: 5 null, 1 true, 0 false; R7 red)
  AC-6  exactly one build sentence, distinct per case, silent when current; `Tick in flight · deploy` ... YES (12 reasons all have prose; an unknown reason names itself)
  AC-7  IMAGE_INPUTS == Dockerfile COPY set, cardinality asserted first, throws on unrecognised forms ... YES (7 COPY lines / 9 sources asserted before any comparison; 8 unrecognised forms all throw; R1/R2/R3 red)
  AC-8  self-restart proven live ................................................ NO — UNPROVEN, ROUTED TO CTO (see below)
  AC-9  one observed end-to-end unattended run .................................. MET ON RECORD, PARTIALLY CORROBORATED BY ME (see below)
  AC-10 no deploy while a tick runs; lock taken with source 'deploy' ............ YES as written (R9 red; loop-label pins `Tick in flight · deploy`) — with finding F5 against its spirit
  AC-11 dirty image inputs -> noop/inputs-dirty, no spawn ....................... YES
  AC-12 exit 0 with a mismatched re-probe is 'fail'/id-mismatch ................. YES (R8 red; and I OBSERVED IT LIVE — see below)
  AC-13 zero deps, zero files outside apps/chat, zero .lattice, no top-level md .. YES (package.json unchanged; watcher imports node:fs/child_process/crypto/path/url only; 11 files all under apps/chat/; `git diff --name-only master...branch | grep -c '^.lattice'` = 0)
  AC-14 suite green in the sanctioned runner, count stated against 255 .......... YES (283/283; +28)
  AC-15 every section-6 guard proven by breaking it ............................. MET AS WRITTEN — 9/10 red, and section 6 pre-authorised reporting R10's green as a finding about that test rather than adjusting it. Recorded as F1.

AC-8 — WHAT I COULD ESTABLISH FROM ARTIFACTS, WITHOUT PROBING
I did not attempt the launchd probe; the classifier has blocked it for two people and I was told not to burn the review on it. From read-only artifacts:
  - `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.american-software.advance-watcher.plist` has `<key>KeepAlive</key><true/>` — a PLAIN BOOLEAN, not a `{SuccessfulExit: ...}` dict. Under plain KeepAlive:true launchd relaunches on ANY exit status, so on THIS host the non-zero exit is not load-bearing at all; exit 70 is protective only against a future plist that used `{SuccessfulExit: false}`. That is a narrowing worth having: the design is correct under both, and the installed plist is the permissive one.
  - `launchctl print gui/503/com.american-software.advance-watcher`: state running, pid 90824, `runs = 7`, `last exit code = 0`, `minimum runtime = 10`. Seven relaunches have happened; every one followed a clean exit, so none of them evidences the non-zero path. Confirms Lena's reading.
  - `minimum runtime = 10` is launchd's default ThrottleInterval, which independently answers the restart-storm question: even a pathological self-restart loop is bounded to one relaunch per 10 s, and the real bound is one per `deployPollS` (60 s) because baselineDigest is recaptured at every startup from the same on-disk file it just restarted for.
  - `ps eww -p 90824` shows the watcher's real env carries HOME=/Users/forrest, USER, LOGNAME and TMPDIR even though the plist declares none of them — so the scrubbed env performDeploy hands docker is viable (docker's CLI-plugin and context lookup both need HOME).
  STILL UNOBSERVED: whether launchd relaunches after a non-zero exit. Owen reserved this ruling; it stays his.

AC-9 — WHAT I CORROBORATED AND WHAT I DID NOT
I did not reproduce AC-9 end-to-end. Two reasons, both deliberate: putting unmerged branch code in front of the board on 8347 is not a reviewer's call either, and reproducing it on an isolated stack requires publishing a host port, which section 6 forbids. I verified instead that the live 8347 container was pre-AS-75 before my incident (`GET /api/build` -> 404 "No such endpoint"), which is consistent with Lena's statement that she deliberately did not deploy to 8347.
What I DID observe live, driving the real makeDeployOps with real git, the real /usr/local/bin/docker and the real runDockerCompose:
  - `resolveDockerBin` -> /usr/local/bin/docker, reason `candidate`, with no plist edit — the plan's central bet, confirmed.
  - `resolveGitBin` -> /usr/bin/git; `computeDesired` -> {"id":"8f75a62d3434de37","dirty":false} over exactly 9 ls-tree lines from the real repo. I independently confirmed the live count is 9 and the tree is clean over those nine paths.
  - `docker compose config` under EXACTLY the scrubbed deploy env (env -i, PATH without /usr/local/bin) succeeds and renders `args: {BUILD_ID: <the id>}` — so the env scrub, the absolute-path spawn and the compose long-form all work together off the thin launchd PATH.
  - a real `docker compose up -d --build` ran to exit 0 under that env, the lock was taken and released (file absent afterwards), and deploy-state.json was written with the full shape.
  - AC-12 LIVE, not just in a unit test: with the prober unable to reach the container, exit 0 was recorded as `outcome: 'fail'`, `detail: "id-mismatch (serving nothing)"`, with the 30-minute cooldown armed. "A deploy is not successful because a command exited 0" is true in the real code path, not only in a stub.
The one link I did not observe is the HTTP flip on a reachable container. I accept AC-9 on Lena's record plus the above; the sub-chain either side of that link is verified.

RULINGS ON THE THREE DEVIATIONS
(1) loopStateKey carries build.{id,desiredId,current} but not `reason` — ACCEPTABLE AS SHIPPED. It is plan section 3.6 verbatim, and following the plan rather than redesigning mid-implementation is the right instinct. The residual is real: while `current` stays false, a reason-only transition (stale-build -> cooldown, say) pushes no frame, so the sidebar's explanatory clause can name the wrong remedy until another keyed field moves. It is bounded — every tick start/stop moves `state`, and a page load refetches. Worth noting for whoever picks up the follow-up: `reason` is NOT time-derived, so adding it would cost no per-poll churn; the exclusion buys nothing that excluding `checkedAt` does not already buy. Follow-up, not rework.
(2) deploy-state.json carries desiredReason/runningId/dockerReason beyond section 3.6's list — ACCEPTABLE.
